title: Mushaf or printed al-Ma'idah 5:6
subject: Islamic Studies
source: Seeded from islamic-studies/y7 lesson 11 (Mushaf or printed al-Ma'idah 5:6)
intro: Lesson 11: Wudu: fard, sunnah and what breaks it. To understand which parts of wudu are obligatory, which are sunnah, and what breaks wudu

passage.title: Qur'an, al-Ma'idah 5:6 (translation of the meaning)
paras: O you who believe, when you rise for prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows, wipe over your heads and wash your feet to the ankles.

questions.q: Explain why washing three times is sunnah, not fard.
questions.a: The ayah commands washing, which is done once; the Prophet ﷺ sometimes washed once, twice or three times, so three is sunnah.
questions.model: Point: three times is recommended. Evidence: 5:6 commands washing without a number; the Prophet ﷺ washed once, twice and three times (Bukhari). Explain: once fulfils the command; more follows the Sunnah. Link: fard makes it valid, sunnah adds reward.

questions.q: Name two sunnah acts of wudu.
questions.a: For example: siwak, three times, starting with the right

questions.q: Make a 'wudu guide for a new Muslim' on the pupil PDF: the steps in order, with F (fard) or S (sunnah) beside each, and a box of three things that break wudu.
questions.a: Correct order; fard: face, arms, head, feet (with order and continuity per many scholars); sunnah labelled; breakers correct
questions.model: Teacher writes the first lines: '1 Niyyah and Bismillah (S). 2 Wash hands three times (S).'

questions.q: what should someone do if unsure whether wudu broke?
questions.a: Stay with certainty: wudu remains (Bukhari and Muslim).

questions.q: why might scholars differ on camel meat?
questions.a: They understood the evidence differently: some took the command as obligatory, others as recommended or abrogated.

questions.q: Washing the face in wudu is ...
Back to our ponder: is wudu valid if you miss a sunnah? A fard?
questions.a: Sunnah missed: valid. Fard missed: not valid.
